about.title: About
about.subtitle: virtuallist.io is an independent, open-source benchmark platform for virtual list libraries.
about.what_p1: virtuallist.io measures the real-world performance of virtual list and virtual scroll libraries across React, Vue, SolidJS, Svelte, and Vanilla JS. Every benchmark runs live in the visitor's browser using real DOM operations — no pre-recorded results, no synthetic scores.
about.what_p2: Currently benchmarking {count} libraries. Results from every run are stored anonymously and aggregated to build a statistically meaningful picture of performance across different hardware, browsers, and library versions.
about.neutrality_p1: Every library on this site is treated as an equal. There is one measurement pipeline — benchmarkLibrary() — and every library passes through it identically. No library gets a different warmup, a more forgiving timeout, or a different DOM template. The same 7-element row structure, the same 48 px item height, the same overscan of 5 is applied to every benchmark.
about.neutrality_p2: Execution order is randomised per run with a coin flip to eliminate JIT warmth and garbage-collection bias. The full methodology is published at /methodology.
about.crowdsourced_p1: Every time someone runs a benchmark, the result is silently persisted to a database — no account required, no tracking, no cookies. Over time this builds a dataset of real-world performance across a wide range of devices and browsers.
about.crowdsourced_p2: The aggregated data is queryable via the public API. Confidence indicators show how many runs back each result: high confidence requires at least 20 runs, moderate at least 5.
about.opensource_p: The entire platform — measurement engine, server, adapters, database schema — is open source and available on GitHub. Library authors are encouraged to review the adapter for their library, raise issues if they spot a measurement flaw, and submit pull requests to improve coverage or fairness.
about.privacy_p: Running a benchmark submits anonymous performance data: metric values, item count, browser user agent, CPU core count, screen dimensions, and the stress level used. No IP addresses are stored. No cookies are set. No tracking scripts are loaded. The data is used solely for aggregated performance statistics.

api.title: API
api.subtitle: Query the crowdsourced benchmark database. All endpoints are public, read-only (except the submit endpoint), and return JSON with CORS headers.
api.cors_note: All responses include Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * so the API can be queried from any origin, including browser scripts and local tools.
api.stats_desc: Aggregated statistics for a library — median, mean, p5, p95, stddev, and sample count for each metric, grouped by library version and item count.
api.history_desc: Daily aggregated time-series data for a single metric and library. Useful for drawing trend charts. Results are grouped by calendar day and library version.
api.history_param_days: Lookback window in days, default 90, max 365
api.libraries_desc: All library slugs that have at least one successful run in the database, with version and run count information.
api.summary_desc: High-level counts across the entire database — total runs, unique libraries, first and last run timestamps, top libraries by run count.
api.browsers_desc: Browser breakdown of all stored runs, parsed from user agent strings.
api.ratelimit_p: The POST /api/benchmarks endpoint (used internally by the benchmark runner) is rate-limited to 30 submissions per IP per minute. The read-only GET endpoints have no rate limit.
api.caching_p: GET responses carry Cache-Control: public, max-age=60, stale-while-revalidate=300. Responses are safe to cache for up to a minute; stale responses may be served for up to 5 minutes while the cache revalidates in the background.

contribute.title: Contribute
contribute.subtitle: Add your library to virtuallist.io so the community can compare its performance alongside every other virtual list implementation.
contribute.how_p1: Every library is benchmarked through the same measurement pipeline using a small adapter file you provide. The adapter implements two functions — create() and destroy() — and the engine handles everything else: timing, memory snapshots, scroll measurement, and result storage.
contribute.how_p2: Your library is treated identically to every other library on the site. Same item height, same DOM template, same scroll speeds, same measurement phases.
contribute.req_intro: Your adapter must follow these rules so the benchmarks stay comparable:
contribute.req_height_desc: Use the exported ITEM_HEIGHT constant (48 px). All libraries use the same row height so scroll measurements are directly comparable.
contribute.req_overscan_desc: Use DEFAULT_OVERSCAN (5 items) wherever your library exposes an overscan option, or DEFAULT_OVERSCAN × ITEM_HEIGHT for pixel-based overscan.
contribute.req_template_desc: Use one of the four shared template helpers — do not write a custom item template. All libraries must render the same 7-element DOM structure per row.
contribute.req_destroy_desc: destroy() must fully unmount the component and remove all DOM nodes. Leftover nodes contaminate subsequent measurements.
contribute.step1_desc: Fork github.com/floor/virtuallist.io and clone it locally.
contribute.step2_desc: Add an entry to src/server/registry.ts with your library's slug, name, tagline, ecosystem, npm package name, and GitHub URL. This one change makes the library appear in navigation, the sitemap, and the homepage grid.
contribute.step7_desc: Submit the PR against the main branch. Describe the library briefly and confirm that all four core metrics complete without errors.
contribute.helpers_intro: Choose the helper that matches your library's rendering model. Every helper produces the same 7-element DOM structure — avatar, title, subtitle, badge, and timestamp — so all results are directly comparable.
contribute.helper_react_desc: Returns a React.ReactElement[]. Use for all React-based libraries.
contribute.helper_template_desc: Returns an HTML string (inner content only). Use for libraries with an HTML template callback.
contribute.helper_dom_desc: Mutates a DOM element in place. Use for SolidJS or vanilla DOM approaches.
contribute.helper_html_desc: Returns a complete <div class="bench-item"> HTML string. Use for libraries that require pre-built row strings.
contribute.other_fix_desc: If you spot a bias, an inaccuracy, or an unfair condition in any adapter or in the engine itself, open an issue or submit a fix.
contribute.other_run_desc: The simplest contribution: visit any library's benchmark page and click Run. Every result grows the crowdsourced dataset.
contribute.other_report_desc: If a library's benchmark fails or produces incorrect results, open an issue with the library slug and the error message.
